name: UAE
lead: The UAE is a hot land on the Arabian Gulf. Golden dunes sit beside the world's tallest skyscrapers. Seven kingdoms joined to make one country in 1971. Camels share roads with supercars. Falcons fly over cities that glow in the desert night.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Built on an island in the Gulf

facts.label: Money
facts.sub: Pegged to the US dollar since 1997

geo: The UAE sits between two seas, the calm Arabian Gulf and the wilder Gulf of Oman. Most of it is flat desert. Dunes grow taller than a ten-storey building. Summer heat can reach 50°C.
The rocky Hajar Mountains rise in the east. Wadis (dry riverbeds) flash-flood after rare rains. Abu Dhabi sits on an island, and Dubai stretches along the coast.
animals: The peregrine falcon is the UAE's favourite animal. Falconers train these swift hunters. They dive at over 300 km/h.
Arabian camels once carried everything across the desert. Today they race on special tracks, with robot jockeys! Dugongs, whale sharks, and hawksbill turtles swim in the warm Gulf.
culture: A guest is always offered qahwa (cardamom coffee) and sweet dates. Refusing is rude! Men wear a white kandura and women a black abaya, even inside glass skyscrapers.
Huge TV poetry slams draw millions of viewers. Souqs (markets) buzz with spices and gold. Wooden dhows, once used for pearl diving, still sail at heritage festivals.
history: For thousands of years, Bedouin tribes herded camels here. Coastal people dived for pearls sold as far as India and Europe. Cheap Japanese cultured pearls nearly ruined that trade in the early 1900s.
Oil was found in Abu Dhabi in 1958. Seven sheikhdoms became the UAE on 2 December 1971. In 50 years, mud-brick villages grew into modern cities.
wows: The Burj Khalifa is 828 m tall, the tallest building on Earth.
Palm Jumeirah is a palm-shaped island made from 94 million m³ of Gulf sand.
The UAE reached Mars on its very first try, in 2021.
Abu Dhabi's Louvre is the first universal art museum in the Arab world.
The UAE has no personal income tax.
Emirati falcons carry official passports for trips abroad.
Ski Dubai has real snow inside a mall.

myths.myth: Camels store water in their humps
myths.fact: Humps hold fat, not water. Camels live off that fat when food runs out.

myths.myth: Desert sand is best for building
myths.fact: Wind rounds desert grains too smooth for concrete. Dubai imports building sand.
